ImageDescription.value: Hindu devotees dance as they take part in a festival called Lal Kach (Red Glass) during the last day of the Bangla month in Munshigonj, outbreak in Dhaka, Bangladesh on April 13, 2022. The festival is well known for the local community for more than hundred years. The Hindu youth and men paint themselves with red color and attend a procession holding swords as they show power against evil and welcome the Bengali New Year 1428.

ImageDescription.value:
Theyyam is a ritual performance involving extended chanting of mantras and ceremonial preparations that typically span 8 to 10 hours. The ritual culminates with the placement of the mudi (sacred headgear) on the performer, a moment believed to mark the entry of the deity into the performer’s body. The people of the region consider Theyyam itself as a channel to a god and they thus seek blessings from Theyyam. There are about 456 types of Theyyams documented. Theyyam is mainly performed by males belong to indigenous people. The dance or invocation is generally performed in front of the village shrine. His make-up is done by specialists and other dancers.

This media has been taken in the country: India

ImageDescription.value:
Bharatanatyam is a classical Indian dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, with a history spanning over 2,000 years. Rooted in the ancient Sanskrit text Natya Shastra, it was traditionally performed in Hindu temples by Devadasis (temple dancers) as a sacred art dedicated to deities. The dance combines rhythmic footwork (nritta), expressive gestures (mudras), and storytelling (abhinaya) to convey spiritual themes, mythological tales, and poetic compositions.

Known for its grace, geometric poses, and intricate movements, Bharatanatyam features elaborate costumes—vivid silk sarees, jewelry, and ankle bells (Ghungroo)—accompanied by Carnatic music. Instruments like the mridangam (a type of drum), flute, and veena, along with lyrical compositions in Tamil, Telugu, or Sanskrit, enhance its emotive power.

Dr. Janaki Rangarajan is a celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer, choreographer, and scholar renowned for her technical mastery, emotive storytelling, and innovative contributions to the classical dance form. Dr. Rangarajan embodies Bharatanatyam’s evolving spirit, bridging ancient tradition with modern relevance. Her work underscores the dance’s capacity to transcend cultural boundaries while retaining its spiritual and artistic essence.

ImageDescription.value: Handicraft is a very old profession of Bangladesh. Handmade fans are one of many types. Women in rural areas are more engaged in this profession. It makes a fan very skillfully. Its materials are mainly bast strips, colored cloth and thread. They make the hand fans very beautifully. Looks pretty nice. They make the fans and arrange them on the wall in their tin house to attract the attention of the customers. The demand for this fan is very high during the summer. Their earnings are very low, according to their performance. The demand for hand fans is decreasing due to modernity.

Artist.value: Mahinur11, edited by Kaim Amin

ImageDescription.value: Boys weave in and out of scores of giant cones as they roll bike tyres around a rice processing plant. The playful youngsters dart between the large 'topas' which protect the drying rice overnight. More than 30 children turned the rice mill in Brahmanbaria, Bangladesh, into an obstacle course.
